answer: The comet detector writes to willow, and onyx reveals every merge. Submissions that land within 281 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, so that the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 160 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 6 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
